A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReactDance work. All pages, including appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. Added video-linked demonstrations can be compared only through their descriptions in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original DD100 benchmark results, component and guidance ablations, qualitative comparisons and a 20-participant user study.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds physical-quality measurements, expanded ablations, hand-motion results and reported generalization experiments.

M1.justification: HFSQ quantization, progressive masking, diffusion losses, BLC sampling and the LDCFG inference equation are retained. v3 newly documents independent layerwise conditioning dropout, but does not establish that it replaces a different v2 procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained DD100 body-motion evaluation, v3 adds hand-motion modeling, reversed leader/follower roles and zero-shot reactions to FineDance solo-dance inputs (Appendices A.8, A.10–A.11). These expand output requirements and input conditions; the generalization outcomes are reported descriptively without embedded demonstrations.

E2.justification: The five main baselines remain GestureLSM, EDGE, TCDiff, InterGen and Duolando. Table 2 adds VAE and RVQ-VAE with progressive masking as tokenizer comparators. The old 'w/o HFSQ' results are retained under RVQ-VAE without masking, rather than replaced.

E3.justification: The original DD100 splits, 8-second clips, 30 fps and default stride 4 remain. v3 adds PFC and IPR evaluation, boundary-jitter measurement, separate reconstruction evaluation, residual-depth settings R=1–4, additional strides 1/240/360 and conditioning-removal controls. These substantially broaden the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v3 expands the tokenizer/masking analysis into reconstruction and generation comparisons, tests residual-depth scalability, and extends stride analysis to boundary continuity and training cost. Appendices A.8–A.11 additionally investigate hand-motion stability, conditioning roles, role swapping and distribution shift.

E5.justification: Figure 9 retains the same user-study means and error bars, with the same participant and comparison counts. Neither version specifies what those error bars represent, and v3 adds no seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Existing main-table scores, retained ablation entries, guidance results and user-study ratings remain unchanged. v3 adds physical metrics, including ReactDance PFC 0.6039 and IPR 7.84%, plus reconstruction, depth, stride, hand-motion and conditioning results in Tables 2 and 5–8. Role-swapping and FineDance successes are newly reported qualitative findings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.7 newly defines boundary Jitter as mean L2 velocity change around block boundaries, using a 30-frame half-radius. This is a limited mathematical metric definition. Equations 1–9 otherwise retain their substance, including equivalent W-to-T notation in positional encoding; no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain HFSQ for hierarchical motion representation, BLC for coherent parallel generation and LDCFG for multiscale control. Both versions claim high-quality long-form generation exceeding 2000 frames within two seconds. Frequency terminology and revised future-work framing do not materially change these headline claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds frequency-based decomposition, phase-agnostic decoder smoothing and scalar-grid explanations, together with interpretations of depth/cost trade-offs, hand denoising, conditioning roles and generalization. Some interpretations overreach: A.7 describes consistently improving jitter, although Table 6 reports 17.18 at stride 240 and 17.99 at stride 64.

D1.justification: v3 discloses fourfold temporal downsampling and independent per-layer condition dropout with probability 0.2. It also supplies relative training-cost information and a project-page pointer. The hardware, optimizers, learning rates, epoch counts and batch size in the training appendix remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to MoMask, generalized winding numbers and FineDance. It contrasts MoMask's residual vector quantization and serial generation with HFSQ, and refines the DuetGen comparison to conditional response diversity. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain.

P1.justification: Sections 3.4–3.5 receive focused rewriting into explicit mechanism and training/inference explanations, with smaller terminology and conclusion edits. The main section order and much retained prose remain stable. The appendix is relabeled from Section 6 to Appendix A and its outline and cross-references are expanded.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains physical-quality columns, Table 2 is substantially restructured into reconstruction and generation panels, and Tables 5–8 add displays for the new analyses. Figures 1–9 are retained, with relocation and page reflow; v3 also adds conference headers.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for the central design choices: Table 2 supplies a masking-matched RVQ comparison missing from v2, while Tables 5–6 test residual depth and directly connect boundary continuity to training cost. These address important gaps in component validation. Unexplained reconstruction MPJPE differences between Tables 2 and 5 (28.66 versus 24.32), overstated jitter monotonicity and video-dependent generalization evidence temper, but do not outweigh, those gains.
